messages.author: 013f68888118cc4c
messages.subject: libraries not loading
parts:
I am running Ubuntu 10.10 and have rapache working. ie I can make R
output on web pages. But I cannot seem to load libraries or install
packages. My normal R terminal has many packages installed. But,
whenever I call library() or require() through rapache I get an error.
For example, when My rapache R function has
require(diagram)
I get the error:

<!--
Loading required package: diagram
Error in consort.dia(screened, eligible, neligible, interested,
ninterested, :
could not find function "openplotmat"
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In rnorm(1000, 0, x) : NAs produced
2: In library(package, lib.loc = lib.loc, character.only = TRUE,
logical.return = TRUE, :
there is no package called 'diagram'
Traceback:
2: consort.dia(screened, eligible, neligible, interested,
ninterested,
consented, nconsented, treat, control) at Consort.R#134
1: main()
-->


In the R console the library loads fine. My main suspect is that I may
have two versions of R installed? When I was installing Rapache a
while ago I seem to remember compiling R with shlibs enabled? I know I
had R installed from the ubuntu repos before that. This may have
produced the two Rs. How do I check that and how do I point Rapache to
the 'correct' R?
Thanks for any help,
Seth Latimer

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: libraries not loading
parts:
Do you really need two R installations? Take a look at RApache info
page, and take a look at R path. Try recompiling RApache with proper R
version.

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: libraries not loading
parts:
It's more a permission issue than Ubuntu issue. If you don't have write permissions in .libPaths[1], then R will try installing into local (/home/<user>/) folder, as Jeroen explained. You can add yourself to the "staff" group which has write permissions to site-library folder:

# adduser <yourusername> staff

and you should add also www-user (or nouser) to the group if you want to install packages from webapp. Then it's up to you... think like admins do. Take it easy on the root priviledges... =)

You should check this one:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3487329/installing-r-packages-available-for-all-users

but please avoid my "neat" solution... "to make errors is human, but to really screw things up, you need root access".

messages.author: 013f68888118cc4c
messages.subject: Re: libraries not loading
parts:
This all has been very helpful. Especially the StackOverflow link.
My first path for both root and user were: 

> .libPaths()[1]
[1] "/home/seth/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/2.11"

So the packages went there whether I started R with root or user, even
when root has permissions to /usr/lib/R/library. I do not know how I
have managed to get this behavior in R. I seem to find many ways of
messing things up. Again this has been super helpful,
Seth
